name: WISE 0855-0714
blurb: The coldest known brown dwarf (about 250 K), moving 8.1 arcsec per year. The challenge coordinates are its 2010 WISE position; by 2026 it is 2 arcmin further west.

target.name: WISE 0855-0714
target.source: Luhman 2014; Luhman & Esplin 2016. Epoch 2010.4 is the mean WISE epoch of the designation; our own SPHEREx detection confirms it.

candidates.note: 3 detections on a line (rms 3.3 arcsec) in pass 2; expected chance alignments in this pass: 3.2

motion.method: zero-sum Gaussian matched filter on per-pass stacks of detectors D5+D6; shift-and-stack of pass-difference maps along the catalogue track; noise = robust scatter over the field

catalogue.source: Luhman 2014; Luhman & Esplin 2016. Epoch 2010.4 is the mean WISE epoch of the designation; our own SPHEREx detection confirms it.

notes: Flux and S/N are from the direct per-pass stacks at the fitted peak (a peak flux is biased high by roughly one sigma); the pass-difference maps prove that the source moves, but their passes are not independent.
Headline motion: joint fit of a moving point source to the pass-minus-mean images (static sources cancel exactly). The centroid-based fit is kept as 'centroidFit'.

measured.model: moving point source fitted jointly to the pass-minus-mean images; catalogue parallax assumed

parallax.note: Annual term 741 +- 408 mas against a catalogue parallax of 433 mas: no annual term is detected above 3 sigma. 3 passes leave 1 degree(s) of freedom.

centroidFit.model: proper motion with the catalogue parallax removed

notes: The combined statistic (6.6; 6.5 at the catalogue position without a search) is not a Gaussian sigma: on random tracks in the same maps it scatters by 0.63. Empirical false-alarm probability: 1 of 2000 random tracks reach the value at the catalogue position, 0 of 200 reach the maximum of the 8-pixel zero-point search. Reversed track: -4.1.

A static source of 277 +- 26 microJy at 0.74-2.4 micron lies within the PSF of the track (the target itself is dark there). It inflates the direct-stack flux and S/N and dilutes stack centroids; only the moving-source numbers (pass differences, joint fit) describe the target.

Flux and S/N are from the direct per-pass stacks at the fitted peak (a peak flux is biased high by roughly one sigma); the pass-difference maps prove that the source moves, but their passes are not independent.
Headline motion: joint fit of a moving point source to the pass-minus-mean images (static sources cancel exactly). The centroid-based fit is kept as 'centroidFit'.
science.verdict: WISE 0855-0714: moving source detected in D5+D6 pass-difference stacks, combined statistic 6.6; not a Gaussian sigma: random tracks scatter by 0.63, 1/2000 reach it at a fixed position and 0/200 with the search (395 +- 69 microJy), 1.5 arcsec from the catalogue prediction; measured 7.81 +- 1.57 arcsec/yr at PA 278.2 +- 4.3 vs catalogue 8.15 at 274.8

notes: false = detections per usable frame outside the excluded radius around the target; positivePerFrame counts positive detections only.

falsePlain uses one purely statistical sigma for all three modes (no star-noise term and no model-error map for the template); falsePlainModelError (template only) is the earlier asymmetric number, statistical sigma plus the template's model-error map.
falsePairCalibration (template only) gives the template exactly the pairs' calibration: the fitted star-noise term without its model-error map.

snrWidth = robust width (1.4826 MAD) of the S/N outside the target mask on faint sky (static sky < 3 sigma), mid (3-10) and bright (> 10 sigma) pixels, classes defined on the chromatic template; 1.0 means a calibrated sigma. falseUnitMad = false detections after dividing each class of each mode's S/N by that width.
depth = median 1-sigma of the difference image in microJy per 6.15 arcsec pixel.
completeness: fraction of injected point sources recovered; 'all' counts frames without a result as misses, 'searchable' leaves them out.
